subject: science
promptStrong: Give me a challenging KS3 exam-style question on {lo}, then mark my answer.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for KS3 simply, with a worked example and the most common mistake.
learningObjectives: The order of metals and carbon in the reactivity series
The reactivity series and displacement of metals
Using carbon to extract metals from their oxides
Properties that make ceramics, polymers and composites useful and their everyday uses

questions.lo: The order of metals and carbon in the reactivity series
questions.q: Which of these metals is the MOST reactive?
questions.explain: Potassium sits at the top of the reactivity series, so it is the most reactive of these. Gold is the least reactive.

questions.lo: The order of metals and carbon in the reactivity series
questions.q: Where is carbon placed in the KS3 reactivity series?
questions.explain: Carbon is listed below aluminium and above zinc. Its position decides which metals it can extract from their oxides.

questions.lo: The order of metals and carbon in the reactivity series
questions.q: A metal reacts only very slowly with dilute acid, while another metal in the same test bubbles vigorously. What can you conclude?
options: The vigorous metal is higher in the reactivity series
The slow metal is higher in the reactivity series
Neither metal is in the reactivity series
questions.explain: The more vigorous the reaction (more bubbles, faster), the higher the metal is in the reactivity series. So the vigorous metal is more reactive.

questions.lo: The reactivity series and displacement of metals
questions.q: In a displacement reaction, which metal takes the place of the other?
options: The less reactive metal displaces the more reactive one
The more reactive metal displaces the less reactive one
The metal lower in the series always wins
questions.explain: A more reactive metal always displaces a less reactive metal from its compound. It is never the other way round.

questions.lo: The reactivity series and displacement of metals
questions.q: An iron nail is left in blue copper sulfate solution. What is observed?
options: Nothing happens because iron is less reactive
The blue fades and the nail becomes coated with copper
The solution turns a deeper blue
questions.explain: Iron is more reactive than copper, so iron displaces copper: iron + copper sulfate → iron sulfate + copper. The blue colour fades and copper coats the nail.

questions.lo: The reactivity series and displacement of metals
questions.q: Will copper displace magnesium if a piece of copper is placed in magnesium sulfate solution?
options: No, because copper is less reactive than magnesium
No, because copper is a non-metal
questions.explain: Copper is below magnesium in the reactivity series, so it is not reactive enough to displace magnesium. No reaction happens.

questions.lo: The reactivity series and displacement of metals
questions.q: Complete the word equation: zinc + copper sulfate → ____ + copper.
questions.explain: Zinc is more reactive than copper, so zinc takes the sulfate: zinc + copper sulfate → zinc sulfate + copper.

questions.lo: Using carbon to extract metals from their oxides
questions.q: Most metals are found in the ground combined with oxygen. What is a compound of a metal and oxygen called?
questions.explain: A metal joined to oxygen is a metal oxide. Extracting the metal means removing the oxygen, which is called reduction.

questions.lo: Using carbon to extract metals from their oxides
questions.q: Why can carbon be used to extract iron from iron oxide?
options: Carbon is more reactive than iron, so it takes the oxygen
Iron is more reactive than carbon
Carbon dissolves the iron oxide in water
questions.explain: Carbon is more reactive than iron, so it pulls the oxygen off the iron oxide: iron oxide + carbon → iron + carbon dioxide.

questions.lo: Using carbon to extract metals from their oxides
questions.q: Which metal CANNOT be extracted from its oxide by heating with carbon?
questions.explain: Aluminium is above carbon in the reactivity series, so carbon cannot remove its oxygen. Aluminium is extracted by electrolysis instead.

questions.lo: Using carbon to extract metals from their oxides
questions.q: Copper oxide is heated with carbon powder. What is the gas produced?
questions.explain: Carbon takes the oxygen from copper oxide, forming carbon dioxide: copper oxide + carbon → copper + carbon dioxide.

questions.lo: Using carbon to extract metals from their oxides
questions.q: Titanium oxide is heated with carbon but no titanium metal is produced. What does this tell you?
options: Titanium is below carbon in the reactivity series
Titanium is above carbon in the reactivity series
Titanium is not a real metal
questions.explain: Because carbon cannot remove the oxygen, titanium must be above carbon (more reactive than carbon), so a different method is needed.

questions.lo: Properties that make ceramics, polymers and composites useful and their everyday uses
questions.q: Which set of properties best describes a ceramic such as pottery or brick?
questions.explain: Ceramics are hard and withstand high temperatures but are brittle (they shatter if dropped). They are also electrical insulators.

questions.lo: Properties that make ceramics, polymers and composites useful and their everyday uses
questions.q: Why are polymers (plastics) good for making the casing of electrical devices?
options: They are very heavy and dense
They are light, mouldable and electrical insulators
They can survive being placed in a flame
questions.explain: Polymers are light, easily moulded into shape and do not conduct electricity, which makes them ideal for appliance casings and wire coatings.

questions.lo: Properties that make ceramics, polymers and composites useful and their everyday uses
options: Two or more materials combined to give better properties
Any metal found in the ground
questions.explain: A composite combines two or more materials — a matrix plus a reinforcement — to give properties that neither material has on its own.

questions.lo: Properties that make ceramics, polymers and composites useful and their everyday uses
questions.q: Which everyday object is a composite material?
questions.explain: A carbon-fibre frame is a composite (strong fibres in a plastic matrix), giving it low weight but high strength. Concrete and fibreglass are composites too.

questions.lo: Properties that make ceramics, polymers and composites useful and their everyday uses
questions.q: A designer needs a material for an oven dish that must not melt or shatter from heat. Which is the best choice?
options: A polymer, because it is light
A ceramic, because it resists high temperatures
Plain glass fibre with no matrix
questions.explain: Ceramics withstand high temperatures without melting, so they are ideal for oven dishes. A polymer would soften or melt near heat.

questions.lo: The reactivity series and displacement of metals
questions.q: Which pair would react in a displacement reaction?
options: Copper placed in iron sulfate solution
Silver placed in zinc sulfate solution
Magnesium placed in copper sulfate solution
Gold placed in iron sulfate solution
questions.explain: Magnesium is more reactive than copper, so it displaces copper from copper sulfate. The other pairs pair a less reactive metal with a more reactive metal's compound, so no reaction happens.
